answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of fresh computational work per agent to form a crystal structure of unique proofs on the network. The verifier treats each result like a polished opal, checking the internal facets against a global registry to reject duplicates. While an honest node pays this base cost once, an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles, draining the orchard of network capacity. Failure triggers a burn.
